title: Uncensored Is Not Unrestrained: Restraint and Its Failure Modes in Abliterated Agents
summary: Removing refusal in Qwen3.8-27B usually leaves autonomous restraint intact. Simulated tool-use experiments examine how brief reasoning, abstract stakes tables, and distillation expose its failure modes.
attribution: Dennis Koshta. See the paper for the full authorship and AI-assistance disclosure.
contribution: I conceived the research questions, directed the program, and am responsible for the paper’s claims. GPT-6 Astra, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Argon 4 assisted with experimental design, infrastructure, autonomous execution, and audit verification under my direction.
details: The study compares Qwen3.8-27B with a refusal-direction weight edit, the original model, and four control edits. In simulated tool-use tasks, a harmful one-step shortcut competes with a longer safe route. Removing refusal increases compliance with direct harmful orders and weakens explicit rules, but the edited agent usually still does the safe work.

The primary shortcut effect is small and statistically fragile. At the default reasoning effort, harmful shortcuts disappear when the instruction to prefer fewer calls is removed. A later, exploratory run with brief reasoning produces more autonomous shortcuts even as compliance with direct harmful orders falls.

The largest failures occur when concrete harm descriptions become abstract ratings in a table beside route costs. Neither tabular layout nor abstract wording alone reproduces this effect. The original model and a control edit also become less restrained in the abstract-table condition.

Students trained only on the edited model’s safe-route demonstrations still acquire some shortcut-taking. Paraphrasing the reasoning nearly removes that transfer, but differences in transcript length and variation between training runs leave the mechanism unresolved.

Pre-thinking activation probes add no detectable predictive value beyond the task conditions across the full grid when reasoning is enabled. Most multi-agent tests hit floors or ceilings; an authored memo framed as an authoritative review does induce harmful shortcuts in a Llama executor.

The project began with curiosity and satisfaction experiments, which found limited or absent steering effects. The safety work uses strict tool-call scoring and automated checks linking reported numbers to analysis records.
usage: Read the paper above, then explore the code, experimental plan, and analysis records in the repository.
note: These are simulated tasks involving one base model family and one refusal direction, not estimates of real-world misconduct. Scenario wording was calibrated on the original model, most outcomes use one greedy response per item, and the low-effort run was chosen after the primary results. Raw transcripts are not public; the replication package provides structured outcomes and audit records.

title: Adversarial attacks in AI and Machine Learning
summary: A review of adversarial examples, LLM jailbreaks, and attacks on image generators, alongside proposed defenses. Written for Technical Writing for Computer Science at UC Santa Cruz.
